blockers.quote: Last line inside the image: tonight, let one thing go
blockers.why: Check #12. This is a lesson in the imperative, not one real line inside the last image. It also advises ('let one thing go') where the outline says mental health is explained, never advised. As spoken, it reads as a moral.
blockers.fix: Make the last spoken line a concrete image beat, in Arthur's dry, warm voice: "The tea's still hot. You drink it." The pages settle on the desk. Say nothing about letting go; the picture of the old shout going quiet carries it.

suggestions.quote: you'll forget it all after anyway
suggestions.fix: Keep it as the spoken habit line but cut it to the way a student mutters it: "I'll forget it all after anyway." Direction: wry, tired. It is the plant for line 35, so Arthur shouldn't lean on it.

suggestions.quote: people with highly superior autobiographical memory
suggestions.fix: Too long for one breath at 1.1x, and it reads like an essay. Say "people who remember almost every day of their lives." Add to say.yaml if the full term is ever spoken: highly superior autobiographical memory -> "HIGH-lee soo-PEER-ee-er aw-toe-bye-oh-GRAF-i-kal memory". Direction: curious, quiet.

suggestions.quote: Every argument with everyone, kept for eighty years.
suggestions.fix: Say the number as words, "eighty years" (a story number). Break it for the voice: "Every argument. Everyone. Eighty years." Direction: hushed.

suggestions.quote: Jill Price's own words about living with her memory
suggestions.fix: Add to say.yaml: Jill Price -> "jill PRICE". Give the quote a separate take with a different emotion (flat, tired) so it doesn't sound like Arthur's narration.

suggestions.quote: forgetting was how you two forgave each other
suggestions.fix: Keep this as the landing line, a complete thought, and don't add a follow-up explanation. Direction: warm, slow, a beat of room before the choice line.

suggestions.quote: Every page, every password, every jingle from every ad.
suggestions.fix: Good rhythm. Direct it as amused, a little faster, so the freeze that follows hits harder.

suggestions.quote: You snap at mom over something from years ago; she doesn't remember it at all.
suggestions.fix: Split it into two takes for the voice: "You snap at her. Over something from years ago." then "She doesn't remember it. At all." Direction: hushed, then quietly stung. This is the cost line and needs its own take.
